stem: A kidney waitlist candidate with coronary risk factors has a positive cardiac stress test during pre-transplant evaluation. What is the MOST appropriate next consultation step?

options.text: Referral to a cardiologist for further evaluation, including cardiac catheterization
Proceed directly to the operating room without additional cardiac workup
Remove the candidate permanently from consideration without cardiology input
Defer all cardiac evaluation until five years after transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Patients with a positive stress test should be referred to a cardiologist for further evaluation, including cardiac catheterization, before transplant clearance.

rationale_incorrect.B: A positive stress test requires cardiology evaluation rather than proceeding without further workup.
rationale_incorrect.C: Positive stress testing triggers further evaluation; it does not automatically confer permanent ineligibility without specialist assessment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cardiac evaluation is part of pre-transplant clearance, not deferred until years after transplant.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Patients with a positive stress test should be referred to a cardiologist for further evaluation, including cardiac catheterization

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → J. Consultations → 1. Cardiac evaluation → d. (positive stress test cardiologist referral); PDF p. 33 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Seventh 020100 item; cardiac consult angle distinct from evaluation protocols (cctc-2017); anchor verified on Cupples p. 33.

stem: During multidisciplinary transplant evaluation, which specialist consultation may be required based on transplant team recommendations beyond the core evaluation protocol?

options.text: Cosmetic dermatology specialist for elective procedures only
Sports medicine specialist for performance enhancement

explanation.rationale_correct: Additional medical consultations may be required based on transplant team recommendations, including infectious disease specialist, cardiologist, psychologist, and anesthesiologist as indicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Elective cosmetic dermatology is not among the standard additional consultations cited for transplant evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Sports medicine for performance enhancement is not a standard transplant evaluation consultation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Veterinary medicine is not part of human transplant evaluation consultations.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Other medical consultations may be required … Infectious disease specialist Cardiologist

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → b. Evaluation process → viii. (additional consultations including infectious disease specialist, cardiologist, psychologist); PDF p. 97 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 020200 item; multidisciplinary consult angle distinct from support resources (cctc-2031); anchor verified on Cupples p. 97.

stem: After initial transplant evaluation, the interdisciplinary team cannot determine candidacy because outstanding studies remain incomplete. How should the coordinator document and communicate the team's recommendation?

options.text: The team is unable to make a determination and further evaluation is required
The patient is approved and will be listed immediately without additional testing
The patient is permanently ineligible and should not return for follow-up
The patient may self-list on the national waitlist without program action

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation outcome communication includes informing patients when the transplant team is unable to make a determination at that time and further evaluation is required.

rationale_incorrect.B: Incomplete evaluation precludes immediate approval and listing without outstanding workup.
rationale_incorrect.C: Indeterminate evaluation requires further workup, not permanent ineligibility without team review.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist registration occurs through the transplant program after a suitability determination, not by self-listing.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: unable to make a determination at this time and further evaluation is required

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.iii. (unable to make determination; further evaluation required); PDF p. 101 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 020300 item; indeterminate-evaluation angle distinct from approved (cctc-2029) and not-listed (cctc-2017); anchor verified on Cupples p. 101.

stem: A lung transplant program receives a deceased-donor organ offer through the allocation system. When presenting the offer to the on-call physician team, which recipient factor should the coordinator include alongside donor quality data?

options.text: The recipient's current condition and availability
Only the donor's social media activity history
Only the recipient's unrelated prior surgical scars
Only the transplant center's cafeteria menu for the week

explanation.rationale_correct: The on-call team considers organ offers in terms of donor factors, recipient factors such as the recipient's condition and availability, and logistical factors including ischemic time.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donor social media history is not part of standard offer presentation factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Unrelated prior surgical scars are not the primary recipient factor described for offer decisions.
rationale_incorrect.D: Center cafeteria operations are irrelevant to organ-offer clinical decision-making.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §8. Organ allocation → f.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: considers the organ offer in terms of donor factors … recipient factors (e.g., recipient's condition and availability)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §8. Organ allocation → f. (on-call team considers donor factors, recipient condition/availability, and logistics); PDF p. 101 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 020600 item; lung offer-presentation angle distinct from DonorNet (cctc-2015) and refusal codes (cctc-2004); anchor verified on Cupples p. 101.
